summary: Verification integrity is mostly honest: every archived number I could recompute matches the instrument that produced it. The 337 #[test] / 1 #[ignore] count equals the reported 336 passed + 1 ignored; the 1207 stress cases are exactly 636+246+200+120+5 with the ~4000 rapid-fire transport sends genuinely counted as assertions and genuinely labelled as transport in both evidence.json and the brief; the region-upscale test really does fill dst with 0xA5 and assert bit-exact equality inside clipped rects (including 1px and corner rects) plus untouched sentinel outside; the leak gate is a single implementation with a passing 19-fixture offline selftest including a negative control that still hides leaks under the old arithmetic, and stress.txt's baseline-collapsed 32 MB numbers match that code; the mutation gate's control and its three catches reproduce. 33d1b9f did not relax a bound: it took SETTLE_MS 150 -> 0 and retargeted the motion selftest expectation in the same commit, and motion.py reads MORPH_DURATION_MS/SETTLE_MS out of src/morph.rs so the instrument grades the shipped 233/0. Acceptance latency is correctly not presented as presentation latency, and the two acknowledged limits (motion recorded pre-theme, CPU figure not a distribution) are labelled in the brief itself. What keeps it off a 9 is reproducibility: two headline claims are true but no committed script can re-run them. I confirmed the GTK3 and GTK4 CSS parse cleanly (0 parsing-error signals, with a deliberate bad color proving the check is sensitive), and I confirmed the theme claim's browser half is scripted, but nothing in the tree performs the GTK half. The CC CPU figure's self+child sampler does not exist at all: the only CPU sampler reads utime+stime and VmRSS of one root pid over 2 s. Plus stale rationale text (EaseOutCubic) against shipped EaseOutQuad, evidence quoting 363 ms bounds while the shipped defaults say 230/260, an unimplemented drop-all mutation in the mutation gate's docstring, and one comment that claims accepted sends are not tests while they do count toward the 1000 gate. None of these invert a pass verdict.

findings.title: Headline GTK3/GTK4 CSS parse claim has no reproducible artifact
findings.detail: The brief states the GTK 3 and GTK 4 CSS were parsed without errors in separate processes. I verified it manually in throwaway interpreters: the live generated dynamite-rust/theme/gtk.css loads through Gtk.CssProvider with zero parsing-error signals on both GTK 3.24 and GTK 4.24, the user gtk.css with its single @import resolves to zero errors, and a control file with '@define-color bogus notacolor;' correctly raises 'notacolor' is not a valid color name, so the check is sensitive to real errors. But nothing in the repo performs it: searching scripts/ and deploy/ for CssProvider, gi.repository, gtk3, gtk4 or GTK_THEME returns no hits, and scripts/theme_selftest.py covers only file-level idempotence/BOM/backup/disable plus the browser screenshot assertion at (350,200)/(60,180). So the GTK half of the theme claim is verified by nobody and a reviewer cannot re-run it. The claim is true; its provenance is missing. Fix is small: in scripts/theme_selftest.py, for each of gtk-3.0 and gtk-4.0, build a temp XDG_CONFIG_HOME, run --apply-theme NAME, then load both gtk.css files with Gtk.CssProvider in a GTK 3 and a GTK 4 subprocess and assert zero 'parsing-error' signals.

findings.title: CC CPU headline (52.0% -> 2.83% of one core, self+children) has no script that can reproduce it
findings.detail: The brief, evidence and COUNCIL_LOG all report a 6 s sample of CC settled CPU dropping from 52.0% to 2.83% of one core, self plus child. The only CPU sampler in the tree is scripts/measure.py:41-57 proc_stats(), which reads utime+stime from /proc/PID/stat fields 13 and 14 for a single root pid chosen by pgrep -x, over a 2.0 s window, with VmRSS rather than Pss. There is no cutime/cstime term and no sum over children anywhere (searching cutime, cstime, ps --ppid, pgrep -P across the repo returns nothing), and no stored command line or transcript for the 6 s run. So the self+child figure, which the sample's whole point rests on, cannot be re-derived from the repo; the shipped sampler would measure the wrong quantity. evidence.json already flags it as 'not a full benchmark distribution', so this is a provenance gap, not a false claim. Fix: add scripts/measure.py --pid-tree that sums utime+stime (and cutime+cstime, or /proc/*/stat children) over the supervisor's descendant set, print the exact command and window used, and store that command next to the 52.0/2.83 figures.

findings.title: Archived rationale says EaseOutCubic, shipped and tested code is EaseOutQuad
findings.detail: Both morph branches set Easing::EaseOutQuad (src/main.rs:5664 and :5698) while the surrounding comments still say EaseOutCubic in BOTH directions (iter33) (src/main.rs:5677, doc at :1084) and motion.py, evidence.json and the archive repeat EaseOutCubic at motion.py:54, :1073, :1081, :1228, :1236 and evidence.json:104,112. Thresholds are unaffected because both curves are monotone with no overshoot, so reversals_max 1 and overshoot_max 0.05 still hold and the pass verdict stands. But anyone reading why the gates are safe is reading about a curve that no longer ships, which is exactly the class of drift this lens exists to catch. Fix: correct the four comment sites and the two evidence strings to EaseOutQuad.

findings.title: Evidence quotes 363 ms bounds while shipped motion.py defaults are 230/260 ms
findings.detail: evidence.json records latency_ms and settle_ms budgets as <= 363 ms and settle_duration_ms as <= 363 ms, but scripts/motion/motion.py:58-60 ship settle_bound_ms 260.0, settle_duration_ms 230.0 and latency_bound_ms 260.0. The run is not wrong: motion.py:696-699 recomputes both from anim_ms + capture median interval + 30, which yields 363 for that capture, so the archived number is the bound actually applied. The problem is that the archived rationale cannot be checked against the committed constants without reading the recompute path, and the two resolved=false gates (latency_ms, settle_ms) contribute nothing, leaving settle_duration_ms as the only live timing gate at 216.8 <= 363. Fix: print the recomputed bounds and their inputs into evidence.json so the 363 is self-explaining, and resolve or drop the two dead gates.

findings.title: Mutation gate docstring advertises a drop-all mutation it never runs
findings.detail: scripts/stress/mutation_gate.py:10-12 describes a drop-all case (every state word swallowed, so state_machine should fail) but the cases list at :95-98 contains only drop calendar, drop lock and slow 3000 ms. So the gate's advertised coverage is wider than its actual coverage, and mutation.txt's PASS silently corresponds to three mutations, not four. The three it runs do catch real breakage (16, 15 and 121 failures), so the gate is not vacuous, but a reader budgeting confidence on the docstring overstates the evidence. Fix: implement drop-all or delete the line.

findings.title: Stress comment claims accepted sends are not tests while they count toward the 1000-assertion gate
findings.detail: scripts/stress/stress.py:1398-1400 comments that the owner's gate is >=1000 genuine assertions rather than >=1000 sends, because a datagram returning ok is not a test, yet :848 increments out.asserts += 1 for every accepted or backpressured send in the four 1000-send rapid-fire loops, and MIN_ASSERTS is 1000. The gate is still met honestly because 6179 minus roughly 4000 transport assertions leaves about 2179 semantic ones, well above 1000, but the comment and the code disagree, so the gate cannot be audited from the comment. Fix: count transport assertions in a separate field and gate on the semantic subtotal, or amend the comment to state that transport assertions count.

findings.title: Archived run artifacts carry no commit id or binary identity, and pids differ from the live-verification record
findings.detail: stress.txt reports pid 20517 while evidence.json's live_verified_executable records pid 12168, and none of stress.txt, mutation.txt, render.txt or halo.txt records the implementation commit or the binary inode/digest it ran against. Motion is separately flagged as recorded before theme integration. I therefore cannot prove from the archive that the 1207-case result belongs to implementation 33d1b9f3; I can only prove the numbers agree with the code that is currently in the tree. Fix: have each script stamp git rev-parse HEAD plus the binary's digest into its report header, and re-run the reports against the candidate commit.

what_would_make_it_a_10: Close the two reproducibility gaps and clear the drift. Add the GTK half of the theme test to scripts/theme_selftest.py: for gtk-3.0 and gtk-4.0 in separate GTK 3 and GTK 4 subprocesses, load the generated gtk.css through Gtk.CssProvider after a real --apply-theme run and assert zero parsing-error signals, plus one deliberate bad-color negative control (I confirmed the check is sensitive and that the shipped CSS passes, so this is about making it re-runnable, not about fixing a failure). Add a pid-tree CPU sampler to scripts/measure.py that sums utime+stime (and children) across the supervisor's descendants, and store the exact command, window and output beside the 52.0 -> 2.83 figures so the self+child headline is re-derivable. Have every stress/render/halo/motion report stamp the implementation commit and binary digest, and either re-run the archived reports against 33d1b9f3 or state plainly which commit each belongs to. Then sweep the stale prose: EaseOutCubic to EaseOutQuad at src/main.rs:5677, :1084 and motion.py's four sites and the two evidence strings; print motion.py's recomputed 363 ms bounds with their inputs into evidence and resolve or delete the two dead gates (latency_ms, settle_ms); implement or delete the drop-all mutation at scripts/stress/mutation_gate.py:10-12; and settle the transport-assertion accounting in scripts/stress/stress.py:1398-1400 against :848 by gating on a semantic subtotal rather than on a total that includes ~4000 sends.
